metadata.claim_supported: The SSR tag renderer iterates the module list when building the opening tag, so the registered `domProps` module is executed during SSR output generation.
metadata.why_relevant: This shows where the server renderer invokes each module while serializing an element's start tag.

metadata.claim_supported: The SSR `domProps` module special-cases `textarea` `value` and turns it into a text child without filtering out falsy values such as `null`.
metadata.why_relevant: This is the code path that can place `null` into a textarea's rendered content.

metadata.claim_supported: Server-side rendering of string nodes converts non-raw text with `escape(String(node.text))`, so a `null` text child becomes the literal string `null`.
metadata.why_relevant: This explains why a textarea text child created from `null` is emitted as `null` in HTML.

metadata.claim_supported: Normal SSR attribute rendering suppresses falsy values, which contrasts with the textarea `domProps.value` path.
metadata.why_relevant: This provides surrounding behavior for ordinary attributes and helps isolate the textarea-specific `domProps` path.
